main_issue: Whether and when Agent D may cook strong-smelling salted fish in the shared flat. Agent D ends up agreeing to cook it only on weekends, with a heads-up to B.

A-B.evidence: A (T1) and B (T2) both complain about the smell. A accepts weekends (T7) and B accepts weekends (T10, T41). Neither addresses the other directly.

A-C.evidence: C complains about the smell in the laundry (T3), then agrees to weekends (T14), the same arrangement A accepted (T7). They never address each other.

A-D.evidence: A asked for no strong-smelling cooking (T1). D first offered advance notice, which A rejected (T5). D then offered weekends only (T6) and A accepted (T7).

B-C.evidence: B (T10) and C (T14) both accept weekend cooking. They never speak to each other.

B-D.evidence: D agreed to B's request for notice (T11, T15). B accepted weekends with notice (T10) and later said 'Okay' (T41).

C-D.evidence: D asked C for agreement (T11). C replied 'weekends are fine' (T14). D confirmed 'weekends it is' (T15).
